radiology_report:
Subject: Prostate mpMRI | Date: 10 February 2025 | Department: Radiology

Clinical indication: A 66-year-old gentleman presents for re-evaluation of suspected clinically significant prostate cancer, following previous positive biopsies. Current PSA measures 13.5 ng/mL.

FINDINGS:
The gland occupies 29.86 mL. T2-weighted sequences highlight a 14 x 12 x 10 mm hypointense focus within the right mid-gland peripheral zone. Diffusion-weighted imaging demonstrates pronounced restriction with correspondingly low ADC values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences reveal early focal enhancement within that same area. No extraprostatic extension, seminal vesicle invasion, or suspicious pelvic lymphadenopathy is identified. Limited field of view imaging shows no osseous abnormalities.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right mid-gland peripheral zone.
Prostate volume 29.86 mL, PSAD 0.452 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.8947026.

previous_notes.author: Dr. F. de Boer (GP)
previous_notes.text: Clinical review focused on a progressive PSA trajectory. A biopsy conducted in 2023 established ISUP GG1 disease. Subsequent testing in June 2024 yielded a PSA reading of 12.3 ng/mL, which triggered further urological referral. The individual remains on tamsulosin for lower urinary tract symptoms and maintains stable COPD management via tiotropium.

previous_notes.author: Dr. F. de Boer (GP)
previous_notes.text: Initial PSA elevation noted during a March 2023 consultation led to serial monitoring. A November 2023 recheck returned 17.8 ng/mL, prompting a transrectal ultrasound-guided sampling. Pathology from that session returned Gleason 3+3, ISUP GG 1. Routine laboratory rechecking was scheduled alongside standard symptom tracking.
